subject: Creativity
title: Positive Mood and the Broaden-and-Build Theory
description: A 60-second lesson on Positive Mood and the Broaden-and-Build Theory.

hook.text: Happy people are measurably more creative. Barbara Fredrickson's research explains exactly why.

buildup.text: Her broaden-and-build theory: positive emotions widen the scope of attention, thought, and action.

discovery.text: Studies show people in positive moods see more peripheral visual information and make more remote associations.

twist.text: Negative emotions narrow focus — useful for detail work but terrible for creative ideation.

climax.text: Even mild positivity (a funny video, a small gift) measurably improves creative problem-solving scores.

punchline.text: Joy doesn't follow creativity. It fuels it.

quiz.question: According to broaden-and-build theory, what do positive emotions do?
options: Widen the scope of attention, thought, and action

details.summary: Barbara Fredrickson's broaden-and-build theory explains how positive emotions expand cognitive repertoire. Good moods broaden attention, increase openness to new ideas, and build lasting intellectual resources. Positive emotions literally widen the range of thoughts and actions that come to mind.
details.whyItMatters: Broaden-and-build provides scientific backing for creating positive work environments. It shows that mood management is not soft management; it directly affects the cognitive resources available for creative work.
takeaways: Positive emotions broaden attention and thought repertoire
Happy moods increase openness to novel and unconventional ideas
Negative emotions narrow focus, which helps survival but limits creativity

faq.question: Does this mean negative emotions kill creativity?
faq.answer: Not entirely. Negative emotions narrow focus, which is useful for certain creative tasks like editing and error correction. But for generating new ideas and making novel connections, positive mood states consistently outperform negative ones. Both moods serve different creative functions.

faq.question: How can you use this practically?
faq.answer: Create positive conditions before creative brainstorming sessions. Brief activities that elevate mood, such as watching something funny, gratitude exercises, or brief socializing, measurably improve subsequent creative performance by broadening cognitive scope.
